ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure first gives an empty 3×3 grid; beside it are shown 4 kinds of available small square tiles. Each kind of square tile is a square divided by a diagonal line into a gray and a white right triangle, and the gray triangles respectively occupy one of the four different corners of the square. The example figure below shows a 3×3 tiling, in which, within a certain 2×2 small grid, the corners of the four gray triangles meet at the center of that 2×2 grid, forming a larger gray rhombus. Then reason: Fix a 2×2 subgrid. To form a large gray rhombus, the directions of the square tiles in these 4 positions are all uniquely determined: the gray corner of each tile must point toward the center of this 2×2 grid. Therefore the probability that a fixed 2×2 subgrid forms a rhombus is (1/4)^4 = 1/256. In a 3×3 grid there are altogether 4 2×2 subgrids. Different 2×2 subgrids cannot all form this kind of rhombus at the same time, because a certain small square they share would be required to have the gray triangle located at two different corners, a contradiction. So these 4 events do not overlap with one another. The total probability is 4 × 1/256 = 1/64.

raw_record.question_text: Each square in a $3 \times 3$ grid is randomly filled with one of the $4$ gray-and-white tiles shown in the image. What is the probability that the tiling will contain a large gray diamond in one of the smaller $2\times 2$ grids? An example of such a tiling is also shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First identify from the image that the four allowed tiles are the four possible orientations of a gray right triangle occupying one corner of a square. A large gray diamond in a 2x2 block requires the four tiles in that block to have their gray corners all meeting at the central point of the 2x2 block, as illustrated by the example. There are four possible 2x2 subgrids in a 3x3 grid. For any fixed 2x2 subgrid, all four tile orientations are forced, so its probability is (1/4)^4 = 1/256. Show that two different 2x2 subgrids cannot both contain such a diamond, because a shared square would need its gray triangle at two different corners. Therefore the four events are disjoint, and the probability is 4 * 1/256 = 1/64.
